So this was an issue I dealt with just today. My desktop at home is running a Windows 10/Gentoo dual-boot which has been working without issues for awhile. I recently had Windows 10 decide to die on me, it would show the loading screen and then a black screen for the login screen. None of the fixes online resolved it so I just reverted back to the most recent restore point. This resolved the blank screen issue but brought forth a laggy system, slow login and broken start menu. It turns out (if you've decided to check Event Viewer by this time) that the Start Menu info is stored in a database file in your user profile. Below are the steps to resolve this issue if it occurs to you :

  • Press Ctrl+Shift+Esc to open up Task Manager, select file, "Run new task", and enter "powershell", run it as Admin.
  • Type in "net user /add fixaccount1" and then "net user /add fixaccount2".
  • Sign out and sign in to fixaccount1, open start menu to ensure it works.
  • Sign out and sign in to fixaccount2.
  • Navigate to C:\Users\fixaccount1\AppData\Local\TileDataLayer\Database and copy the vedatamodel.edb file to the user account with the broken start menu, same location (C:\Users\$brokenuser\AppData\Local\TileDataLayer\Database) and delete the "EDB.log" and "EDBtmp.log" files in the broken user directory folder as well.
  • Sign out and sign in the broken start menu account.
  • Verify it works, delete the two fix accounts however you prefer to.

If this helps you, let me know. I tried fixing the database using eseutil but that wasn't of much use. It seems like you need to copy the database from a good user and delete the transaction logs in the folder as well.

So in my abnormal psychology class, I've learned about "the 4 d's of abnormality", which include:

Deviance, dysfunction, distress and danger.

*Deviance is deviation from the norm. Different, extreme, unusual or bizzare.

A) Thoughts, behaviors and emotions are different from what is considered normal in a specific time or place by people.

B) the individual deviates from social norms which are stated and unstated rules for proper conduct in a given society or culture.

C) judgments of abnormality vary from society to society as norms grow from a particular culture. They so depend on circumstance.

*distress - being unpleasant or upsetting to the person

A) according to clinical theorists, behaviors, thoughts, and ideas have to cause distress before they're considered abnormal. Other theorists may not believe this.

*dysfunction - refers to the interference in a person's ability to conduct daily activities

A) abnormal behavior leads to interference in daily functions. Culture and play a big role. Some examples of dysfunction are as follows:

Social isolation, fear, not eating, less sleep, increased appetite, fear, not eating, depression, down mood, self conscious, hygiene, thinking too much, joy, paranoia, hyperactivity, decrease in motor functions,

And finally we have danger - person poses risk or harm

A) abnormal behaviors become dangerous to one's self or others - behaviors may become careless, hostile or even confused

B) dangerousness tends to be exception rather than rule
